# Best portable power station for camping

The best pick depends on how much you need to run. Most campers are well served by a small 250-300Wh unit, and a bigger one only makes sense for fridges or multi-day trips.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (about $249) is PowerStationGearLab's top pick. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4, weighs 8.3 lb, and has a 300W output. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so it's mainly sold through Amazon and other retailers. [Details and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (about $269-299) has 286Wh and a 600W inverter, and it can expand to 572Wh. It's the best value if you want more output. [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (about $199) has 288Wh, a built-in lantern, and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard AC model, not the "C300 DC" variant. [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (about $179) is the budget pick, with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. [Same guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Longer trips, a 12V fridge, or van and overland use
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** was OutdoorGearLab's best for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh, a 2,200W output, and weighs 39 lb. The list price is $1,499, but it was reported under $900 on sale. It's not enough for a space heater or multi-day electric cooking. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 on sale. It has a 1,800W output and weighs 25 lb, but its fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (about $799) has 1,070Wh and 1,500W, and it's TechRadar's pick for camping. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** was WIRED's best for camping at $1,079-1,199. It's IP65-rated, weighs about 40 lb, and has 1,536Wh. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Mid-size option with a current code
**Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh, an 1,800W output, and weighs about 16 kg (35 lb). It lists at $499, and Dealectric reports that code AFF5OFF took $24.95 off in Bluetti's cart on 2026-10-21, bringing it to about $474. That's an affiliate link, and checkout has the final word on price. It has no expansion port, and the $599 listing is a bundle with a solar panel. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

## My take
For most campers I'd choose the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** or the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**. Choose the EcoFlow if you want more AC output or room to expand. If you need a fridge or more days of power, step up to the Anker C1000 Gen 2 or the Bluetti AC180.

Reviewers don't fully agree on the small units. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker SOLIX C300 (50) fairly low in its lab tests, while PowerStationGearLab ranked them at the top for camping. Their picks also lean toward weight and simplicity over raw performance.

Prices change often, so check the current price before you buy. Most of these links go to review pages with buy buttons, since I only had direct store links for the Bluetti.
